{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-de-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"2392f3c4556b4568d614c35edea562a45b009c28f10170058a6960eefb692d52","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-de-class-d:lineage:23","source_registry_sha256":"7b6c7aeec232df29a8679bf39181604be2d91ce9a1cb4fcc709fed49cbe724bb","source_liveness_sha256":"53bd779b9965bd9d51630c8d8d055ccdc52a4d8ec7117a3b87241fc5129eb44f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Revocation, suspension and driver improvement","heading":"C — Revocation, suspension and driver improvement","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Revocation, suspension and driver improvement

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
The handbook lists driving under the influence of liquor or narcotic drugs among mandatory revocation grounds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Hit-and-run driving that involves another person’s injury or death is listed as a mandatory revocation ground. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Trying to flee after a police officer gives a visible or audible vehicle-stop signal is listed as a mandatory revocation ground. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Three reckless-driving convictions within 12 consecutive months are listed as a mandatory revocation ground. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
Causing or contributing to a person’s death through vehicle operation is listed among mandatory revocation grounds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
The handbook lists an assault crime involving death through vehicle operation as a mandatory revocation ground. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
Using a motor vehicle to commit a serious crime is listed as a mandatory revocation ground. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A01
False statements or fraudulent information are included in the handbook’s mandatory revocation list. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A01
Possessing or consuming alcohol while younger than 21 is listed as a mandatory revocation ground. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A01
A person who posts bond after arrest for a listed revocation cause and then fails to appear in court has the license revoked as though convicted. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A01
A driver declared a habitual offender may have the license revoked for as long as five years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A01
A person convicted as a habitual offender cannot receive a work or hardship license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A01
A combination of three listed habitual-offender offenses within five years may lead to a habitual-offender finding. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A01
Manslaughter, using a vehicle for a felony, impaired driving, unlicensed driving, driving during suspension or revocation, and reckless driving appear in the habitual-offender offense list. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A01
The habitual-offender list also includes failure to stop or identify yourself at a crash, a false DMV statement, violating an occupational license, and ignoring a police stop command. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A01
A combination of listed habitual-offender offenses and lesser violations such as speeding that totals 10 convictions within three years may also establish habitual-offender status. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A01
The DMV will suspend a Delaware resident’s license when it has reason to believe the person committed an offense requiring suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A01
The DMV will suspend a Delaware resident’s license when it has reason to believe reckless or unlawful driving contributed to a crash causing injury, death or serious property damage. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A01
The DMV will suspend a Delaware resident’s license when it has reason to believe a serious medical or mental condition makes the person unable to drive competently. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A02
The suspension list includes a serious vehicle-law violation, driving without the owner’s consent, and an uncollectible payment to the DMV. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A02
Racing, spinning wheels, damaging turf or other property, and failure to answer a court summons in any state appear among suspension grounds. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A02
License-related suspension grounds include using a fictitious, borrowed, suspended or revoked license, lending a license, failing to surrender a withdrawn license, and giving false application information. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A02
False insurance documents, driving uninsured or without an insurance card, passing a stopped school bus, and altering or fraudulently using a license are listed suspension grounds. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A02
The suspension list includes failure to pay child support and failure to surrender a vehicle’s plate after canceling its insurance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A02
A person owing at least $1,000 in arrears or retroactive child support and at least 30 days late under a Family Court or Division of Child Support Services order may have the license suspended. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A02
A child-support suspension remains effective until the requesting agency’s release reaches the DMV, and reinstatement requires a $50 fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A02
The Problem Driver Program uses information, training and progressively stronger sanctions to address accumulating convictions or points and prevent crashes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A02
Problem Driver Program actions may include an advisory letter, mandatory suspension, or a behavior-modification or attitudinal-driving course. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A02
Reinstatement after a Problem Driver Program suspension requires a $50 DMV fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A03
Speeding from 1 through 9 mph above the posted limit carries two points in the handbook’s point table. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A03
Speeding from 10 through 14 mph above the posted limit carries four points in the handbook’s point table. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A03
Speeding at least 20 mph above the limit carries five points and may bring additional action, including suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A03
Passing a stopped school bus carries six points and may bring additional action, including suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A03
Reckless driving carries six points in the Delaware point table. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A03
Operating a vehicle in a way that causes death carries six points and may bring additional action, including suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A03
Aggressive driving carries six points in the Delaware point table. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F37 | anchor: A03
Disregarding a stop sign or red light carries three points in the Delaware point table. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F38 | anchor: A03
Other moving violations covered by the cited Delaware traffic-law chapters carry two points in the handbook’s table. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F39 | anchor: A03
For the noncommercial point-action process, the DMV may act when a driver accumulates at least eight calculated points within two years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F40 | anchor: A03
For administrative action, violation points count at full value during the first 12 months and at half value during the next 12 months; this calculation does not apply to CDL holders. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F41 | anchor: A03
A requested driving record displays full-value points rather than the DMV’s internally calculated point value. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]
